title: Small factorization class for compact localization images
statement: For a Grothendieck abelian category A with a v-small derived category, choose the exact compact localization model L : B ⥤ D(A) with compact generating family E. There exist a regular cardinal κ in universe v and an essentially v-small object property G on D(A) such that G is stable under integer shifts, every G-object is κ-small, G is a coproduct factorization class, and every L.obj (E j) belongs to G.

proof.text: Choose B, its compact generating family E, and the exact localization L with fully faithful right adjoint from the compact localization model. Choose a complex representative X_j of each L(E_j).

Fix a separator H of A. Choose a regular cardinal beta larger than aleph_0 and the cardinalities of Subobject(H^(finite coproduct n)) and Subobject(X_j^m), for all j,m,n. Let P consist of complexes generated in each degree by fewer than beta copies of H. The component bounds put all X_j in P. Every member of P is an epimorphic image of the fixed disk copower; it is therefore isomorphic to the cokernel of the inclusion of a subobject of that fixed complex. This proves essential smallness. Shifts only reindex degrees. The Lean helpers bounded_family_cardinal, bounded_complexes_essentiallySmall and bounded_complexes_shift prove these assertions using the existing CardinalGenerated and GeneratingMonoQuasiIsos source-library API.

Every derived morphism QX -> QY with X in P has a roof QT -> QX and QT -> QY with T in P. First replace its denominator s:W->X by the epimorphic quasi-isomorphism W plus mappingCocone(id_X) -> X; the original W is a retract and the new summand is contractible. For an epimorphic quasi-isomorphism p:W->X, use the source-library cover lemma degreewise and close under differentials to find a P-subcomplex T_0 of W mapping onto X. Its kernel embeds in the acyclic kernel of p and is in P by stability under subobjects. Swallow its image in an acyclic P-subcomplex V of ker(p), using CochainComplex.exists_acyclic_degreewiseCardinalGenerated_le. Push out ker(T_0->X) -> T_0 along its map to V. The pushout T is a quotient of T_0 plus V, hence in P, and the short exact sequence V -> T -> X makes T->X a quasi-isomorphism. The compatible map T->W gives the required roof. These steps are fully proved in epi_quasiIso_replacement, bounded_subcomplex_epi, bounded_epi_quasiIso_roof and bounded_derived_roof.

Q preserves the relevant coproducts by the existing derived coproduct cofan proof. For a chain map b:T->coproduct_i Y_i with T in P, take Z_i=image(b followed by the i-th coproduct projection). Each Z_i is a quotient of T, hence in P. In an AB5 abelian category the coproduct projections jointly detect zero: pull back along finite partial coproducts, use their finite projection-sum identity, and use exactness of the filtered colimit. Exactness of coproducts therefore factors b through coproduct_i Z_i. Apply Q and the coproduct comparison to the bounded roof, and transport along the chosen representative isomorphisms. This proves G4 for S=P.map Q. The helpers coproduct_projection_zero, coproduct_component_images and bounded_class_factorization give the full Lean construction.

Choose a common regular cardinal alpha bounding Subobject(T) for a small skeleton of P. For each T in P, the partial coproducts on subsets of cardinality less than alpha form an alpha-filtered diagram of split monomorphisms with colimit the full coproduct. Mathlib IsGrothendieckAbelian.IsPresentable.surjectivity applied with the subobject bound makes every map from T factor through one such partial coproduct. Thus all members of P are alpha-small as complexes. Apply this support factorization to the numerator of the bounded roof and then apply Q; naturality of the coproduct comparison shows every object of S is alpha-small. These are uniform_subobject_bound, alphaSmall_of_subobject_bound and bounded_class_alphaSmall.

Functoriality of Q under shifts makes S shift stable, and ObjectProperty.map preserves essential smallness. The original representatives X_j show that S contains all L(E_j). Combine these properties with the compact localization data; no localizing-generation assertion is used here.

proof_origin.place: Complete bounded-complex and bounded-roof proof, using the proved source-library CardinalGenerated, CardinalGeneratedCover, AcyclicSwallowing and GeneratingMonoQuasiIsos API; no canonical alpha-compact small-class theorem is assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_small_factorization_class_of_compact_localization
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{v} A] :
    ∃ (B : Type (max u (v + 1))) (cB : Category.{v} B),
      letI := cB
      ∃ (zB : HasZeroObject B) (sB : HasShift B ℤ) (pB : Preadditive B),
      letI := zB
      letI := sB
      letI := pB
      ∃ aB : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor B n).Additive,
      letI := aB
      ∃ tB : Pretriangulated B,
      letI := tB
      ∃ (iB : IsTriangulated B) (sumsB : HasCoproducts.{v} B),
      letI := iB
      letI := sumsB
      ∃ (J : Type v) (E : J → B),
        (∀ j, IsCompactObject (E j)) ∧ IsTriangulatedGeneratingFamily E ∧
        ∃ (L : B ⥤ DerivedCategory A) (R : DerivedCategory A ⥤ B)
          (adj : L ⊣ R) (sL : L.CommShift ℤ),
          letI := sL
          L.IsTriangulated ∧ IsIso adj.counit ∧
          ∃ (G : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory A)) (κ : Cardinal.{v})
            (_ : Fact κ.IsRegular),
            ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.{v} G ∧ G.IsStableUnderShift ℤ ∧
            (∀ U, G U → IsAlphaSmall U κ) ∧
            G.IsCoproductFactorizationClass ∧
            ∀ j, G (L.obj (E j))
